subtitle: Lesson 3 · Chapter 1: Product Category Performance Snapshot

eyebrow: FROM and JOIN -- the plan, in SQL
code:
FROM Sales.SalesOrderDetail AS sod
JOIN Sales.SalesOrderHeader AS soh
    ON sod.SalesOrderID = soh.SalesOrderID
JOIN Production.Product AS p
    ON sod.ProductID = p.ProductID
JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory AS psc
    ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = psc.ProductSubcategoryID
JOIN Production.ProductCategory AS pc
    ON psc.ProductCategoryID = pc.ProductCategoryID
caption: Five tables, four join keys, exactly like the Lesson 2 plan.

code:
WHERE soh.OrderDate >= DATEFROMPARTS(
    YEAR(GETDATE()),
    (DATEPART(QUARTER, GETDATE()) - 1) * 3 + 1, 1)
  AND soh.OrderDate < DATEADD(MONTH, 3, DATEFROMPARTS(
    YEAR(GETDATE()),
    (DATEPART(QUARTER, GETDATE()) - 1) * 3 + 1, 1))
caption: A half-open range: on or after quarter start, before next quarter starts.

eyebrow: SELECT, GROUP BY, and the DISTINCT count
code:
SELECT
  pc.Name AS CategoryName,
  SUM(sod.LineTotal) AS TotalSalesAmount,
  COUNT(DISTINCT soh.SalesOrderID) AS OrderCount
...
GROUP BY pc.Name;
caption: DISTINCT matters: joins repeat each SalesOrderID once per line item.
